observation.visible_scene: A close view of the flat dark-gray top of a stove-like metal appliance, with a black cylindrical flue pipe rising from the center-back and a small brass circular fitting on the front lip. The background is horizontal wooden paneling. On the left portion of the top there is a white wet-looking patch with a horizontal streak, and the rest of the surface is dotted with scattered small white specks. A thin black cable is partly visible at the left edge. Wispy vapor/steam hangs around the pipe base and drifts across the right side of the top.
visible_changes: An upward spray/fountain of fine droplets above the left white patch grows taller and denser over the segment, becoming most pronounced in the later frames.
The left white patch brightens and appears to spread/expand slightly as the spray intensifies.
The scattered white specks on the surface persist but their pattern shifts subtly, consistent with droplets landing and boiling.
The vapor/steam continuously swirls and drifts upward and toward the right around the pipe.

The camera framing slowly shifts leftward (a pan/zoom-out), progressively revealing more of the left edge, the black cable loop, and a pale wall/door at the far left; the pipe moves toward the right side of the frame.
The brass fitting and the pipe remain fixed relative to the stove top throughout (object positions stable; apparent motion is camera-driven).
outside_clip_unknowns: What produces the spray and the white patch (pouring, boiling liquid, sputtering, etc.) is not shown.
Whether the spray was already active before the first frame or continues after the last is unknown.
The material identity of the white patch and the specks is not determinable from the images.
uncertain_details: Direction of the left-edge droplets (ejected upward vs. falling) cannot be confirmed frame-by-frame.
Whether the surface motion is camera pan or a slight physical shift of the appliance is inferred from background change; the relative leftward reveal is clear but the mechanism is not.
The exact growth of the white patch vs. mere brightening from lighting/spray overlap is hard to separate.
